exemplars.title: Spellburst: A Node-based Interface for Exploratory Creative Coding with Natural Language Prompts
exemplars.why: Spellburst makes persistent alternatives the interface itself: artists create variation branches in a node graph and can merge paths without destroying their separate histories.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It outranks Branchat because it supports both forking and recombination in a visible node graph, demonstrating a richer form of branching exploration than conversation-tree navigation alone.

exemplars.title: Branchat: A Tree-Structured Interface for Efficient Revisitation in Long-Horizon LLM Conversations
exemplars.why: Branchat provides an unusually precise fork operation: users can select any retained conversation node as a parent and spawn a divergent branch within a tree designed for later revisitation.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It outranks ImaginationVellum because the evidence identifies the exact user control and parent-child operation used to create a branch, whereas ImaginationVellum's navigation and display mechanics are less fully specified.

exemplars.title: ImaginationVellum: Generative-AI Ideation Canvas with Spatial Prompts, Generative Strokes, and Ideation History
exemplars.why: ImaginationVellum lets users return to different previously generated designs and grow new variation branches from each, preserving multiple visual lineages as live source material on an ideation canvas.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It outranks -generAItor because its evidence explicitly shows user-created forking from retained alternatives, while -generAItor clearly exposes a beam-search tree but does not establish an equally explicit path-creation control.

notes: I departed from the consensus by moving rid 10375 (-generAItor) out of the final three and elevating rids 9118 and 13801. The visible beam-search tree in -generAItor is compelling, but the supplied evidence emphasizes inspecting, explaining, and adapting a model-generated tree rather than explicitly creating and switching among user-controlled branches, leaving part of the structural signature unverified. I raised Branchat by 0.15 and ImaginationVellum by 0.05 because their evidence more directly establishes nondestructive forking from retained prior states; no adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should still be cautious that the short excerpts do not independently document every required control: Spellburst's abstract does not explicitly describe active-path switching, Branchat's excerpt does not state that all branches are simultaneously displayed, and ImaginationVellum's excerpt leaves canvas navigation mechanics implicit.
